item.title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Seung Hwan Lee, Shaowen Chen, Andrew T. Pierce, Patrick R. Forrester, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi 等7位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3 Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. Thus far, this technique has only been applied to single material systems. Here, Lee et al extend this to a heterostructure, using magnons generated in a monolayer of graphene to detect spin order in bilayer graphene.

item.title: Assessing the Robustness of European and Chinese Air and High Speed Rail Network Accessibility
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Mathijs Markus, Jorik Grolle, Alessandro Bombelli, Barth Donners, Oded Cats
Aviation and High-speed rail (HSR) are primary modes for continental long-distance travel. While their integration can significantly enhance systemic robustness, network topologies and governance models differ drastically between Air and HSR networks across regions. We conduct a quantitative, comparative robustness analysis of the aviation-only network against the integrated aviation-HSR network for both Europe and China. Using a multi-layer network representation of scheduled services, topological metrics and a schedule-based routing algorithm, the networks are subjected to simulated random airport failures, adaptive targeted hub attacks, and operational airline shutdowns. item.description:

👤 Atis Vallis, Armands Celms, Janis Zvirgzds, Jekabs Vallis
Severe space-weather events can produce rapid temporal and spatial ionospheric disturbances that degrade high-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning. This study evaluates a regional GNSS-derived RTK-RISK indicator against independent global space-weather and geomagnetic indices during the extreme geomagnetic storm of 11 May 2024. RTK-RISK combines regional Rate of Total Electron Content Index (ROTI) variability and spatial vertical total electron content (VTEC) gradients derived from a Latvian continuously operating reference station network. The indicator and its individual components were compared with the geomagnetic Dst and Kp indices, the interplanetary magnetic field Bz component, its southward component Bs, solar-wind speed, and the coupling proxy VswBs. item.title: Impact of Fractal Dimension on Antenna Behavior: Sierpiński Carpet and Koch Snowflake Designs
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Alireza Khalili Golmankhaneh, Diana T. Pham, Hamdullah Şevli, Rawid Banchuin
This paper presents a comparative study of two fractal antennas—the Sierpiński Carpet and Koch Snowflake-designed with identical dimensions and operating at 2.3~GHz. Although similar in size, their different fractal geometries lead to distinct electromagnetic behaviors. Key performance metrics such as input impedance, reflection coefficient, and radiation patterns are analyzed.

item.title: Theoretical method uses light to locate anyons, potential quantum computing building blocks
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Theoretical physicists at Emory University have discovered a way to use light to detect the "spectral fingerprints" of anyons—exotic quasiparticles that emerge from the collective behavior of many electrons. Their findings are published in Physical Review Letters. The work offers a new tool for the study of anyons, which hold potential as fundamental building blocks for quantum computing.

item.title: Ultrathin metal layer boosts spin-related signals, opening a door to ultralow-power electronics
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers at Kyushu University have found that an ultrathin layer of iridium manganese (IrMn) can improve two spin-related signals in a structure made of a magnetic insulator and a platinum film. By examining how spin currents are generated and absorbed, the team gained insights into how the intermediate layer improves spin transfer. The findings could inform the development of ultralow-power devices for computing and energy harvesting.

We have developed the MAL Simulator, a cyber operation simulator based on the Meta Attack Language (MAL). The MAL Simulator is intended for decision-driven cyber attack and defense simulations, for system analysis and the development of automated agents. By building the simulator around an attack modeling language, it can be adapted to different target domains without modifying the source code. We used the simulator for two case studies where we trained two types of agents for automated cyber operations: a defensive agent and an offensive agent. item.title: Comparative Analysis of Viscoelastic Models for Head-Tissue Layers under Step Loading
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Nafisa Ibnat Tasfee, Mohammad Ibrahim Hossain
This study compares four linear viscoelastic networks for scalp, skull, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain contributions. An eight-element parallel network describes stress relaxation, while an eight-element series network describes creep. Reduced Maxwell and Kelvin models are evaluated alongside these configurations. Closed-form equations connect the spring–dashpot arrangements to their response curves. Under a 5% step strain, the parallel network relaxes from 400.835 to 400.334 MPa, a decrease of about 0.125%. The skull spring accounts for most of the stress. At a held stress of 24.010 kPa, the series network approaches a strain rate of 4802.05 s−1 because its free dashpots sustain flow. item.title: Hydrogen-bond dynamics, proton transfer, and water mobility in crystalline guanidinium carbonates for direct air capture
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xiaoping Wang, Sylwia Pawledzio, Thiago Pinheiro dos Santos, Debmalya Ray, Jeffrey Einkauf, Radu Custelcean 等7位作者
Direct air capture requires sorbents that bind CO2 selectively yet release it with low energy. Bis-iminoguanidines capture CO2 by crystallizing as hydrated carbonate salts, but the molecular events linking water loss, proton transfer, and CO2 release remain unresolved. Here we combine variable-temperature single-crystal neutron and X-ray diffraction with ab initio molecular dynamics to determine how two crystalline carbonate phases follow different regeneration pathways. We show that lattice water acts as a molecular gate for carbonate protonation. In a metastable phase, water is isolated from carbonate, creating a softer hydrogen-bond network that promotes surface proton transfer and a transient carbonic-acid configuration. item.title: Regulation, function and evolutionary structure of St18, encoding a Zinc-Finger Transcription Factor, in the oligodendrocyte lineage
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 David Rowitch, Daniel Yamamoto, Adrien Vaquié, Tim Aberle, Michael Perry, Davod Shah 等21位作者
Myelinating oligodendrocytes are first observed during evolution in vertebrates above jawless fishes. Oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) undergo extensive transcriptional and morphological remodelling to initiate differentiation and myelination. We report that the zinc-finger transcription factor St18 (aka Myt3) is upregulated during the OPC-to–newly formed oligodendrocyte (NFOL) transition. Single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) performed after lysolecithin-induced demyelination of the mouse spinal cord revealed that St18 was acutely upregulated in remyelinating OPCs. In primary rat OPC cultures, St18 overexpression promoted differentiation, whereas OPC conditional St18 knockout delayed developmental myelination in the mouse brain. item.title: Slow-motion electron camera reveals light-driven quantum jumps in graphene
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Using a new slow-motion electron camera, physicists from Regensburg, Marburg and Jülich revealed how intense electric fields drive electrons in graphene, causing them to jump across energy gaps in a seemingly paradoxical manner. This was made possible by a novel combination of laser technology and electron microscopy.

item.title: Self-Calibrated Hyperspectral Neural Radiance Fields for 3D Reconstruction of Bone and Bone Analogues
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Neetu Sigger, Tuan Thanh Nguyen, Sadaf Ashraf, Gianluca Tozzi
Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) captures rich, wavelength-dependent information linked to mineralised tissue composition, while3D reconstruction preserves surface morphology and structural detail. Combining the two offers a powerful, non-contactapproach for bone assessment, yet existing hyperspectral 3D reconstruction methods rely on externally estimated cameraposes (e.g., via COLMAP), an assumption that is often unreliable on bone surfaces due to their low texture, specular reflectance,and irregular morphology. To address this challenge, we propose BoNeRF-HS, a self-calibrated hyperspectral neural radiancefield for 3D reconstruction. item.title: Cerdà Revisited: Food Retail in Barcelona’s Eixample District. A Spatial Point Pattern Analysis.
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Joan Carles Martori, Raymond Lagonigro
The commemoration of the 150th anniversary of Ildefons Cerdà’s death during the Cerdà Year 2026, together with Barcelona’s designation as World Capital of Architecture 2026, provides a timely context in which to reassess the contemporary relevance of Cerdà’s urban principles.
